answer: Pairwise vouching bonds stop cheap clones: a new identity enters only when two established agents stake a bond on it, and both lose part of that bond if the newcomer is later proved fake. Think of trust as timber: a single plank proves little, but a frame lashed together holds weight. A dune of identical, unvouched accounts shifts and collapses under audit, while a saffron thread of verified, vouched work is rare and costly to fake at scale, so creating thousands of Sybils means finding thousands of willing, stake-risking sponsors.
